content:
Translating Sumerian texts can be complex due to the intricacies of the language, and without context for each line, translations may vary. Here is a literal translation attempt based on the provided Sumerian text:

1. "On the day of the festival of the sky and the earth, it has been prepared."
2. "On the day of the festival, the sky and the earth have been celebrated."
3. "On the day, my name has been declared."
4. "The great lord has been invoked."
5. "Dama-Dinana has given an offering."
6. "Dama-Dinana has created the heavens."
7. "Dama-Dinana… has ascended and provided."
8. "The great god has established X in his shrine."
9. "The great god, the mighty, has looked over the territory, the great rebirth has been established."
10. "The great god has made offerings, may it be noted that the sacrifices have been fulfilled."
11. "The great god has commanded and declared his word."
12. "On the day of the celebration, the great god of the skies has been honored."
13. "In the house of the god, the great lord stands; may the god not remove the special offerings."
14. "The great god has taken his place, and issues commands, may it not be forgotten."
15. "The great god has extended his hand; he has provided plenty."
16. "People who have taken their place are joyful, may they not forget their vows."
17. "Dama-Ke4, the mother of the palace, has been invoked during the festival of the great god."
18. "The hearts of the gods have rejoiced and have laughed with joy."
19. "X has blessed both us and you."
20. "X, may there not be…" [unclear part]
21. "They are bringing the offering; may it be accepted; X will see."

Note that some parts may remain ambiguous due to the fragmented nature of ancient Sumerian texts, and the translation relies on interpretations of individual signs and contextual clues.
